_doc: Inflation benchmarks for retrospective editions dated in 2020: the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at each cutoff. End-2019 state of the verified 2019 register (its two 2019 changes, New Zealand's Remit for the Monetary Policy Committee of 14 Feb 2019 and China's ~3% objective of 5 Mar 2019, are the starting rows), updated for the 2020 current-year targets set earlier: Brazil 4.25 → 4.00% ±1.5 (CMN Res. 4,582 of 29 Jun 2017, art. 1 II); Indonesia 3.5 → 3.0% ±1 (PMK 124/PMK.010/2017, Art. 2(3)(b)); Thailand 2.5 → 2.0, the midpoint of the 1–3% headline range agreed by the Minister of Finance and the MPC and approved by the Cabinet on 24 Dec 2019 (BoT MPC announcement No. 3/2562 of 25 Dec 2019, a scanned PDF read from the page images and matched against The Bangkok Insight report of the same day; the BoT's English translation is not cited, its PDF being created later); Türkiye 5% ±2pp (CBRT Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy for 2020, 5 Dec 2019, paras 2–3; its statement that Inflation Report forecasts 'act as interim targets' in periods of significant deviation is recorded in the wording, and the agreed 5% target is used); Colombia 3% with a 2–4% range (Board of 25 Nov 2019; banrep.gov.co sits behind a bot check, so its page was read through a fetch service and the quoted text is from the Ámbito Jurídico copy of the communiqué). Korea's 2% (26 Dec 2018, no fixed period; restated in the BoK's policy direction of 27 Dec 2019) and India's 4% (statutory target notified 5 Aug 2016; same wording in the MPC resolution of 6 Feb 2020) are carried. Changes announced during 2020: Chile's updated framework document (published 11 Feb 2020, reported 12 Feb; value unchanged at 3%, recorded because it replaces the row's wording: the ±1pp range no longer defines the target); China ~3 → ~3.5% from the Report on the Work of the Government delivered 22 May 2020 (the earlier editions keep the 5 Mar 2019 objective); the FOMC's amended Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy of 27 Aug 2020 ('inflation that averages 2 percent over time'; value unchanged, recorded for its wording and cited from the dated press release, because the statement's own page and PDF were modified later). Value-unchanged reaffirmations are not recorded: the UK remit of 11 Mar 2020 ('re-confirm the inflation target as 2 per cent'); India's 2020 MPC resolutions; Korea's two-yearly review of the target's operation. No new Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy was issued in Australia, nor a new remit in New Zealand, during 2020. Targets set during 2020 for later years are not recorded. Every new source was fetched and its quoted text checked; sources are shown only once published; no wording names a later year.
note: Where an official objective refers to an index other than headline CPI (the Federal Reserve's PCE price index; see each row), the benchmark is applied to headline CPI. India's benchmark is the RBI's stated CPI objective for the current period. Benchmarks apply to the headline CPI series used here. Each benchmark is the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at the cutoff; China's is the government's annual CPI objective from its Report on the Work of the Government (until that report, the previous year's applies). Where a range was set, its midpoint is used; for the euro area's ‘below but close to 2%’, 1.9%. Sources are listed only if published on or before the edition’s last eligible day.

US.wording: FOMC Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy, 25 Jan 2012: 'The Committee judges that inflation at the rate of 2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures, is most consistent over the longer run with the Federal Reserve's statutory mandate.'
US.index: PCE price index; benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Federal Reserve press release, FOMC statement of longer-run goals and policy strategy, 25 Jan 2012

XM.wording: 'A year-on-year increase in the HICP for the euro area of below 2%' … 'maintain inflation rates close to 2% over the medium term' (below but close to 2%: 1.9% used).

urls.label: ECB press release, evaluation of the monetary policy strategy, 8 May 2003

JP.wording: 'The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy', 22 Jan 2013: 'the Bank sets the "price stability target" at 2 percent in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index (CPI)' (replacing the 1% 'price stability goal' of February 2012); in the joint statement with the Government the Bank will 'aim to achieve this target at the earliest possible time'.

urls.label: Bank of Japan, The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 22 Jan 2013
Joint Statement of the Government and the Bank of Japan on Overcoming Deflation and Achieving Sustainable Economic Growth, 22 Jan 2013

GB.wording: June Budget 2010: 'the independent Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Bank of England will continue to target 2 per cent inflation, as measured by the 12-month increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI)'.

urls.label: HM Treasury, Budget 2010 (June, HC 61), 22 Jun 2010, para 1.27

CA.wording: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Inflation-Control Target, 24 Oct 2016: 'The target will continue to be defined in terms of the 12-month rate of change in the total CPI. The inflation target will continue to be the 2 per cent mid-point of the 1 to 3 per cent inflation-control range'; the agreement runs for the five-year period that began at the start of 2017.

urls.label: Bank of Canada, Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Inflation-Control Target, 24 Oct 2016

AU.wording: Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 19 Sep 2016: 'They agree that an appropriate goal is to keep consumer price inflation between 2 and 3 per cent, on average, over time' (midpoint 2.5%; the previous Statement said 'over the cycle').

urls.label: RBA Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 19 Sep 2016

CH.wording: The SNB 'regards prices as stable when the national consumer price index (CPI) rises by less than 2% per annum' (midpoint of 0–2%: 1.0%).

urls.label: SNB Quarterly Bulletin 4/2007, 'Inflation forecasting as part of the monetary policy concept'

SE.wording: Riksbank, 7 Sep 2017: 'The Executive Board of the Riksbank has decided to adopt inflation measured in terms of the CPIF (the consumer price index with a fixed interest rate) as a formal target variable for monetary policy. The target for monetary policy is that the annual change in the CPIF shall be 2 per cent, that is, the same level previously applied to the CPI'; a variation band of 1–3 per cent replaces the ±1pp tolerance band, applying from the monetary policy decision of 6 Sep 2017.
SE.index: CPIF (CPI with a fixed interest rate); benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Sveriges Riksbank press release No. 21, 'CPIF target variable for monetary policy', 7 Sep 2017

NO.wording: Regulation on Monetary Policy laid down by the Government on 2 Mar 2018 (in force immediately; the 2001 regulation repealed from the same date), Section 3: 'The operational target of monetary policy shall be annual consumer price inflation of close to 2 percent over time. Inflation targeting shall be forward-looking and flexible so that it can contribute to high and stable output and employment and to counteracting the build-up of financial imbalances.' Norges Bank: 'The inflation target is now 2%, compared with the previous 2.5%.'

urls.label: Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report 1/18, 15 Mar 2018 (reproduces the Regulation of 2 March 2018 on Monetary Policy, p. 13)
Norges Bank, Executive Board's assessment, Monetary Policy Report 1/18, 15 Mar 2018

NZ.wording: Remit for the Monetary Policy Committee, signed 14 Feb 2019 by the Minister of Finance and the Governor and issued to the new Monetary Policy Committee, which makes monetary-policy decisions from 1 Apr 2019 (the remit 'replaces – and is largely the same as – the Policy Targets Agreement'): the MPC's operational objectives shall be to 'keep future annual inflation between 1 and 3 percent over the medium term, with a focus on keeping future inflation near the 2 percent mid-point. This target will be defined in terms of the All Groups Consumers Price Index, as published by Statistics New Zealand; and' (ii) 'support maximum sustainable employment'.

urls.label: The remit for the Monetary Policy Committee, Reserve Bank of New Zealand, signed 14 Feb 2019 (copy published with the interest.co.nz report)
interest.co.nz, 'Robertson defends the independence of the RBNZ as more details on the new committee he'll appoint to set the OCR are revealed', 14 Feb 2019
Good Returns, 'Key RBNZ changes edge closer', 14 Feb 2019

CN.wording: Report on the Work of the Government delivered 5 Mar 2019, main projected targets for this year: 'CPI increase of around 3 percent' ('居民消费价格涨幅3%左右'; a government objective, not a PBoC target; the previous year's was also around 3%).

urls.label: China Daily, 'Main goals for economic and social development in 2019' (from the Report on the Work of the Government), 5 Mar 2019
Report on the Work of the Government delivered 5 Mar 2019 (full text, in Chinese, gov.cn / Xinhua), 16 Mar 2019

IN.wording: RBI Monetary Policy Committee: policy is set 'in consonance with the objective of achieving the medium-term target for consumer price index (CPI) inflation of 4 per cent within a band of +/- 2 per cent' (resolution of 6 Apr 2017, the first after the earlier 5 per cent objective reached its horizon; the same wording in each later resolution, most recently that of 5 Dec 2018). This is the statutory target of 4% with tolerance levels of 2% and 6%, notified 5 Aug 2016.

urls.label: RBI, First Bi-monthly Monetary Policy Statement 2017–18: Resolution of the Monetary Policy Committee, 6 Apr 2017
RBI, Fifth Bi-monthly Monetary Policy Statement 2018–19: Resolution of the Monetary Policy Committee, 5 Dec 2018
Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Finance, 'Central Government in consultation with RBI announces the Inflation Target of Four Percent', 5 Aug 2016

BR.wording: CMN: 'para o ano de 2020, meta para a inflação de 4,00% (quatro por cento), com intervalo de tolerância de menos 1,50% (um e meio ponto percentual) e de mais 1,50% (um e meio ponto percentual)' (4.00% with a ±1.5pp tolerance band).

urls.label: CMN Resolution 4,582 of 29 Jun 2017, art. 1 II (2020 target; published in the DOU of 30 Jun 2017)

MX.wording: 'Annual CPI inflation of 3 percent' with a variability interval of ±1 percentage point.

urls.label: IMF Public Information Notice 07/140, Mexico Article IV, 13 Dec 2007
Banxico Inflation Report October–December 2007 and Monetary Program for 2008

ZA.wording: Budget Speech, 17 Feb 2010: 'I wish to confirm that the Reserve Bank will continue to pursue a target for CPI inflation of 3 to 6 per cent' (midpoint 4.5%).

urls.label: Minister of Finance, Budget Speech 2010, 17 Feb 2010

TR.wording: End-2020 CPI inflation target of 5%, set jointly with the Government: the CBRT's Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy for 2020 (5 Dec 2019), para 2: 'The inflation target has been kept at 5% as per the agreement reached with the government. Monetary policy will be set so as to bring inflation to the target gradually. In periods of significant deviation from the inflation target, the inflation forecasts presented in the CBRT’s Inflation Reports act as interim targets.' Para 3: 'The uncertainty band around the inflation target, is kept at 2 percentage points in both directions same as the previous years.' The agreed 5% target is used; the Inflation Report forecasts are not.

urls.label: CBRT, Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy for 2020, 5 Dec 2019 (paras 2–3)

PL.wording: Continuous CPI target of 2.5% with a symmetric ±1 percentage-point band, restated in the Monetary Policy Council's monetary policy guidelines (resolution of 30 Sep 2009, published 14 Oct 2009).

urls.label: Monitor Polski No. 66, item 868: MPC resolution of 30 Sep 2009 on monetary policy guidelines (published 14 Oct 2009)

HU.wording: 'An inflation rate near the 3 per cent medium term objective.'

urls.label: MNB Quarterly Report on Inflation, November 2007
MNB Quarterly Report on Inflation, February 2008

urls.label: CNB press release, 'The CNB's new inflation target and changes in monetary policy communication', 8 Mar 2007
CNB press release, 'The CNB issues Inflation Report I/2010', 12 Feb 2010 (the new inflation target of 2%)

ID.wording: Inflation target for 2020 of 3% with a deviation of 1%, fixed by Finance Minister Regulation 124/PMK.010/2017 (set and promulgated 18 Sep 2017), Article 2(3)(b): '3% (tiga persen) untuk tahun 2020' … 'dengan deviasi sebesar 1% (satu persen)' (annual CPI inflation, year-on-year, at year-end: 'Inflasi IHK tahunan (year-on-year) di akhir tahun').

urls.label: Peraturan Menteri Keuangan 124/PMK.010/2017 on the CPI inflation targets, promulgated 18 Sep 2017

KR.wording: Price stability target from 2019 set by the Monetary Policy Board on 26 Dec 2018, in consultation with the Government: 2% in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index ('2019년 이후 물가안정목표'를 소비자물가 상승률(전년 동기 대비) 기준 2.0%로 확정 의결), the same level as the 2016–2018 target; the three-year application period is abolished (no fixed period), with the operation of the target reviewed every two years ('3년마다 재설정했던 물가안정목표의 적용기간을 없앴다. 다만, 2년 주기로 물가안정목표 운영 개선에 필요한 사항을 점검키로 했다').

CL.wording: 'Keep annual CPI inflation around 3% most of the time, within a tolerance range of plus or minus one percentage point.'

urls.label: Central Bank of Chile, Monetary Policy in an Inflation Targeting Framework, January 2007

CO.wording: Board of Directors, 25 Nov 2019: 'la Junta Directiva del Banco de la República reitera que su meta de inflación de mediano plazo se mantiene en 3%, en un rango entre 2% y 4%' (medium-term target 3%, range 2–4%) and 'reitera que las acciones de política monetaria están encaminadas a conducir la inflación a la meta del 3% en 2020'.

urls.label: Banco de la República, 'Junta Directiva del Banco de la República reitera que su meta de inflación de mediano plazo se mantiene en 3%' (in Spanish), 25 Nov 2019

TH.wording: Monetary-policy target for 2020 approved by the Cabinet on 24 Dec 2019, as agreed between the Minister of Finance and the Monetary Policy Committee: headline inflation within the range of 1–3 percent as the medium-term price-stability target and the target for 2020 ('รัฐมนตรีว่าการกระทรวงการคลังและ กนง. มีข้อตกลงร่วมกันโดยกำหนดให้อัตราเงินเฟ้อทั่วไปในช่วงร้อยละ 1-3 เป็นเป้าหมายนโยบายการเงินด้านเสถียรภาพราคาสำหรับระยะปานกลาง และเป็นเป้าหมายสำหรับปี 2563'); a range with no point target, replacing the annual average of 2.5 ± 1.5 percent (midpoint 2.0% used).

urls.label: Bank of Thailand, MPC announcement No. 3/2562 on the monetary-policy target for 2020 (in Thai), 25 Dec 2019
The Bangkok Insight, Cabinet approves the 2020 monetary-policy target of 1–3% headline inflation (in Thai), 25 Dec 2019

CL.wording: Updated framework document 'La Política Monetaria del Banco Central de Chile en el Marco de Metas de Inflación' (published 11 Feb 2020): 'El nivel de meta para la inflación está fijado en 3% anual. Ello significa que la política monetaria se orienta a que la variación anual del IPC fluctúe en torno a 3%' and 'El propósito práctico u objetivo operacional de la política monetaria es que la inflación proyectada se ubique en 3% anual en un horizonte de política en torno a dos años' (value unchanged; the ±1pp range no longer defines the target: inflation 'debería fluctuar la mayor parte del tiempo en un rango de entre 2 y 4%').

Banco Central de Chile, 'La Política Monetaria del Banco Central de Chile en el Marco de Metas de Inflación', February 2020 (PDF)

CN.wording: Report on the Work of the Government delivered 22 May 2020: 'China has set its consumer inflation target at around 3.5 percent' for the year ('居民消费价格涨幅3.5%左右'; a government objective, not a PBoC target; the previous year's was around 3%).

US.wording: FOMC Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy as amended 27 Aug 2020: the longer-run goal of 2 percent PCE inflation is kept, and the Committee 'seeks to achieve inflation that averages 2 percent over time', so that 'following periods when inflation has been running persistently below 2 percent, appropriate monetary policy will likely aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time' (value unchanged).
